title: POC weekly: cache warmup & routing tuning
summary: Weekly sync to review KV/prefix cache hit-rate, discuss cache warmup strategy, address routing and fallback behavior, and agree next steps for benchmark run and security doc handoff.
topics: KV vs prefix cache hit-rate trends
next_steps: Redwood to share updated cache warmup config and histogram of prefix lengths (Maya) — by 2026-05-15
Cobalt to run second benchmark with 10k sessions using warmup enabled and share results (Lena) — by 2026-05-20
Jonas to attach tuned routing policy JSON and sample fallbacks to the pilot repo — by 2026-05-14
Redwood to send SOC2 / KMS integration notes to Harold for review — by 2026-05-18
action_items: Maya — compile and send cache warmup config + notes (2026-05-15)
Jonas — upload routing policy JSON and example logs to pilot repo (2026-05-14)
Lena — run 10k-session benchmark with warmup, share metrics and sample traces (2026-05-20)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-12 14:00 UTC | Duration 46m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Lena (ML Eng), Harold (Platform), Sana (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick check — is this still a good time?
[01:00] Lena: Yeah we're good. We pulled yesterday's run, saw a bump in prefix hits after the cache tuning, about — uh — 10 percentage points, but the KV cache numbers are all over.
[02:00] Jonas: Right, so the key thing is the prefix collison — sorry, collision — threshold we set was too strict so it didn't capture near-matches, that hurt the effective KV hit for short prompts.
[03:00] Harold: When you say near-matches, you mean canonicalization? We currently do a lower-case and strip punctuation in our pre-processing, but we don't normalize numbers or date formats.
[04:00] Sana: And for product we care about repeat user flows, like the compare-price and summary flows. We saw big wins in those, maybe 20-30% latency reduction when prefix cached.
[05:00] Maya: Great context. Jonas, can you walk through the warmup strategy you tested? There was an email but not full details.
[06:00] Jonas: Sure. We did a two-stage warmup: lightweight prefetch of top-100 prefixes per minute from your traffic histogram, then KV populate for session anchors. For the test run we used a TTL of 12 hours and async populate so it didn't block the request path. That got prefix hit from ~42% to ~60% overall on the scenario set.
[07:00] Lena: The async populate is interesting. Any observed spike in write IO or memory pressure? Our nodes are pretty memory constrained.
[08:00] Jonas: There was a small memory bump — about 6%. Write IO increase was linear with number of sessions; for your traffic profile it was within safe limits, but if you scale to 5x we'd recommend a burst queue.
[09:00] Harold: Burst queue — is that something Redwood provides or we implement upstream? We want to avoid managing another queue process.
[10:00] Maya: We can provide a managed burst buffer inside Dedicated, but for the hosted pilot we suggested an in-process async batcher. We'll attach a config you can drop in.
[11:00] Sana: On routing — we noticed some requests got routed to the cheaper variant and had a higher token cost due to rollbacks. Can we tighten fallback rules? We need predictable 95th percentile latency.
[12:00] Jonas: Yeah, currently policy is cost-first with latency safeguard. For the pilot I proposed a fine-grain routing policy: route by path, not just model, and pin high-SLO paths to Dedicated; allow fallback only when latency breaches for 3 consecutive samples.
[13:00] Lena: How do you define a path? Our app has dynamic user prompts — do we bucket by intent or exact endpoint?
[14:00] Jonas: Good question. We used intent buckets derived from your event taxonomy (compare, summarize, explain). Intent-level pinning gives most of the benefits without exploding routing rules.
[15:00] Maya: Also worth noting: prefix cache warmup pairs well with intent pinning, because warmup populates the prefixes the pinned route sees.
[16:00] Harold: On security, we have two asks: KMS integration for keys and audit logs including per-request token usage. I shared the audit schema with Maya after the last call.
[17:00] Maya: Yep we got it. For KMS we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS; onboarding requires a CIP (customer integration packet) — we'll send the details and the minimal IAM policy.
[18:00] Sana: We also need to know retention windows. Some of the PII flows will need prompt redaction at ingestion, can Redwood support redaction hooks?
[19:00] Jonas: There's a pre-router hook you can use for redaction; it's invoked before caching. If you redact then the cache keys will reflect redacted content. We should be deliberate about canonicalization so redaction doesn't reduce reuse.
[20:00] Lena: We ran a quick experiment: redacted keys dropped hit-rate by about 8% because our numeric normalization differed. Any suggestions?
[21:00] Jonas: Two things: standardize numeric canonicalization in your preprocessor, and for high-security flows, use session-scoped cache keys to avoid cross-user leakage. Session-scoped gives lower reuse but preserves safety.
[22:00] Maya: Back to metrics — we saw an odd blip around 03:12 UTC where prefix hit dropped to 34% for 12 minutes. That's in the pilot sheet. Any idea what happened?
[23:00] Harold: That timeframe corresponds with a deploy on our side, but we didn't touch the inference layer. There might have been a traffic spike with new prompt variants from a marketing test.
[24:00] Jonas: I pulled logs; there were a sudden set of longer prompts which shifted the KV cache keys because of more unique session context. Our adaptive batching also hit a different kernel path causing a slight perf shift.
[25:00] Lena: So action item — we'll pause marketing test and re-run the pattern after we enable warmup?
[26:00] Sana: Yes, we'll coordinate. Also request: can Redwood provide example TTL bending guidance? For some entities we want shorter TTLs.
[27:00] Jonas: We'll include a TTL guidance doc — typical pattern: entity-level TTLs (user name: 24h, session anchor: 12h, ephemeral tokens: 5m). You can tune by hit-rate curves.
[28:00] Maya: For the next benchmark run, let's agree on these changes: enable async warmup, apply intent-level routing pinning for compare/summarize, and canonicalize numbers in preprocessor.
[29:00] Lena: Agreed. We'll also mask PII and run with session-scoped keys for sensitive flows.
[30:00] Harold: Quick question about observability: can we get token-level breakdown per route and per model variant? We need that to justify Dedicated.
[31:00] Jonas: Yes, Redwood Console can do token breakdown by route and model. For the pilot we'll add a token-level dashboard and share a read-only link.
[32:00] Sana: Competitor note — we briefly estimated Vertex AI cost for this workload. Redwood's warmup + routing approach still looks better on unit economics for 95th percentile latency.
[33:00] Maya: Nice. Anything else on regressions or quality? We ran a small eval suite and saw no measurable quality drop from routing to cheaper variants, but there were edge cases with long-context completions.
[34:00] Jonas: For long-context flows we recommend pinning and increasing KV snapshot frequency — that reduces cold-start token overhead.
[35:00] Lena: Do you have a sample config for snapshot frequency? We'll need that for our infra team.
[36:00] Jonas: I'll push a sample in the repo — snapshot frequency is typically every N=50 tokens or T=30s depending on response lengths. We'll include both templates.
[37:00] Maya: I'll also follow up with the SOC2 docs and the KMS CIP. Harold, expect an email with attachments.
[38:00] Harold: Thanks. Also, can you include example audit log lines? We want to map them into our SIEM.
[39:00] Jonas: Will do. We'll provide sample logs including request_id, route, model_variant, token_count, cache_hit boolean, and trace_id.
[40:00] Sana: One more ask — for product acceptance, we need a regression dashboard comparing baseline vs warmup for CER/accuracy on anchored prompts. Can Redwood compute that?
[41:00] Jonas: We can run automated evals against your labeled test set and produce a delta report. If you share the eval set we'll run it as part of the benchmark.
[42:00] Lena: We'll share the labeled set in the pilot repo by EOD tomorrow.
[43:00] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Maya sends configs and SOC2 packet; Jonas pushes routing and snapshot samples; Lena runs 10k-session benchmark with warmup; Harold reviews KMS/IAM.
[44:00] Jonas: And I'll attach example logs and dashboard link to the repo.
[45:00] Maya: Perfect. Same time next week?
[46:00] Lena: Same time works for us. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end: 14:46 UTC.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and small recognition errors (e.g., 'collison' for 'collision', 'CV cache' once), original audio reference available on request.
